p1: [low, ominous] For seventeen years, the F B I hunted a bomber... [whispers] and the man who stopped him was his own brother.
[low] Nineteen seventy-eight. A bomb at a Chicago university.
[low] Then more. Universities... airlines. [low, ominous] The F B I code-named him... Unabom.
[low] Sixteen bombs. [low, tense] Three people killed.
[low] Then, in nineteen ninety-five, he made an offer.
[low] Publish his thirty-five-thousand-word manifesto... [low, ominous] and the bombings would stop.
[low] The New York Times and The Washington Post printed it.
[low] In New York, a man named David read it... [whispers] and recognized his brother's writing.
[low] April, nineteen ninety-six. Agents surrounded a tiny cabin in Montana. [low, tense] No electricity. No running water.
[low] Inside: forty thousand pages of journals... [whispers] and one live bomb. Ready to mail.
[low, ominous] That bomb never left the cabin... [whispers] because his brother spoke up.
